subject: Prod launch: unexpected backpressure during planned ramp
messages:
From: Liam Parker <liam@brightbox.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Launch Ops <launchops@brightbox.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Load test: starting ramp now — seeing 5xx/429 spikes

Connor —

We're kicking off the planned ramp (see attached ramp-plan-v2.pdf) at 09:10 PT and within ~3 minutes started to see elevated 429s and 5xx errors. Quick snapshot:
- Target peak: 500 rps
- Observed 429s: started at ~09:13, peaked ~12% of requests for ~90s
- 5xx rate: ~4% (mostly 502/503)
- Median latency was normal initially but P95 jumped to ~800ms during spikes

We rolled out no client-side retry changes; traffic pattern is a steady step curve per the attached (first step 50rps -> 100 -> 250 -> 500). I can pause if you need. Logs attached (redwood-logs-brightbox-20260620.zip).

This is blocking our launch rehearsal. Can you triage and get eng/ops eyes on this now? We also need an exec update if this impacts the timeline.

Phone: +1-415-555-0199 (available now)

—Liam
Liam Parker
Director, Platform @ BrightBox
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Parker <liam@brightbox.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 09:23:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test: starting ramp now — seeing 5xx/429 spikes

Liam — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. I'm pausing the ramp on our side for now (confirming with Launch Ops).

Looping in Marissa (runtime/ops) and Evelyn (CS lead) to triage. Initial asks from our side so we can move fast:
- A slice of the traffic curve (CSV) and whether clients used exponential backoff
- Any recent config changes on your side (timeouts/retries) in the last 24 hours
- A link to the ramp plan (I have the PDF but CSV is ideal)

Immediate mitigations we'll try:
1) Reduce concurrency from 500rps target to 250rps and re-run a stepped ramp
2) Disable aggressive client retries to avoid retry storms
3) Marissa is going to check autoscaler metrics and cache hit rates — we'll consider a short pin to a dedicated pool if necessary

Targeting a 09:45 quick triage call. I'm available and will stand up a temporary channel.

—Connor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Liam Parker <liam@brightbox.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 09:35:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test: starting ramp now — seeing 5xx/429 spikes

On Sun, Jun 20, 2026 at 09:23 Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Looping in Marissa (runtime/ops) and Evelyn (CS lead) to triage.

Thanks — I'm on it. Initial telemetry summary from the runtime team (09:30):
- Autoscaler: oscillation seen at node pool level coincident with step increases — instances spun up then drained rapidly (scale up latency + scale down triggers)
- KV/prefix cache: a large number of unique request prefixes generated many cache misses during the first big step; hit rate collapsed from ~92% to ~18% across the cluster
- Retry amplification: a subset of clients were issuing tight retries which amplified load during outages
- Error breakdown: 502/503 dominated; some 429s from the serving layer's token-limiter during enforcer contention

Short-term actions (we're deploying these now):
- Enable temporary burst capacity for BrightBox (pin a small dedicated pool for the next 3 hours)
- Raise token limiter for this customer to reduce 429s while we stabilize
- Apply a rapid cache-warm policy (preload top N prefixes from your sample)
- Throttle/patch autoscaler threshold to avoid immediate scale-down after a transient spike

Please send the CSV for exact curve. If you want, we can also fallback readers to a larger model variant that has more stable latency under load — that would increase cost but reduce 5xx risk.

I'm making Marissa_Cole-incident-20260620 in our incident tracker and will paste the runbook events there.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Liam Parker <liam@brightbox.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Launch Ops <launchops@brightbox.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 09:50:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test: starting ramp now — seeing 5xx/429 spikes

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the rapid response.

We can pause the ramp for now. Attached is the CSV for the intended curve: https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/1A2b3RampPlan/view — first step to 50 rps at 09:10, then 100, 250, 500 over ~20 minutes.

Quick context/questions:
- Our go-live date is scheduled for 2026-06-25 (internal execs are watching this rehearsal)
- We do use client retries but with jitter; we did not change retry config today
- If you recommend fallback to a larger model variant, what's the expected latency/cost delta? We need guidance to present to our Execs

Also want to flag we may request an SLA credit if this was a platform-side shortcoming blocking our rehearsal. Will you escalate to your leadership for an exec update?

—Liam
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Parker <liam@brightbox.com>, Launch Ops <launchops@brightbox.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test: starting ramp now — seeing 5xx/429 spikes

Team — looping in ops leadership.

Thanks for the quick triage, Marissa. Immediate decisions I approve:
- Provision a temporary dedicated pool for BrightBox for the remainder of the day and through Monday morning (costs covered by Redwood for the first 24 hours)
- Raise per-customer token limiter thresholds for the pinned pool to reduce 429s
- Assign Marissa to lead the postmortem; deliverable: timeline, root cause, and a concrete ramp/playbook we give to BrightBox before the next attempt

Connor/Evelyn, please prepare an executive summary for BrightBox with: what happened, what we did in the moment, impact, and what we will do to prevent recurrence (include costs/credits and the recommended ramp schedule). I'm happy to join a call with their execs if they want an escalation-level briefing.

We should also agree on a canary plan (small % of traffic for the first 30 minutes, gradual doubling with 10-minute steady-state checks) and communicate hard gates.

—Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
